rules.statement: Load a recovery or offline-only private key from a file passed explicitly to the offline command, never from configuration, and never register its unwrapper as a service a serving process can resolve (for example as a key wrapper in the serving DI container).
rules.why: Configuration is long-lived and replicated, and the recovery private key must never reach a process that serves.
rules.check: Look for a recovery or offline private key read through IConfiguration or options, or an unwrapper that uses it registered in the host's service collection.

rules.statement: Decrypt unwrapped key material into sensitive buffers that are zeroed after use, not into ordinary arrays or strings.
rules.why: Unwrapped master key material must not stay in memory after it is used.
rules.check: Look for unwrap or decrypt calls that write key material into plain byte[] or string values that are never cleared, instead of a zeroed sensitive buffer.

rules.statement: Require an RSA key of at least 3072 bits imported from a `PRIVATE KEY` PEM for recovery unwrapping, decrypt with RSA-OAEP using SHA-256, derive the key id from the public half, and refuse a wrapped copy that names a different key id.
rules.why: This makes sure recovery uses a strong key and the right padding, and that a copy is only unwrapped by the key it was wrapped for.
rules.check: In recovery-key code, look for a missing key size check, padding other than OAEP-SHA256, a key id taken from input instead of derived from the public key, or no key-id match check before decrypting.

rules.statement: When rewrapping a key, keep its material unchanged and check its key size and key check value after unwrapping and before writing the new wrap.
rules.why: Rewrapping must not change any stored secret, and verifying first stops a corrupt or wrong unwrap from being saved.
rules.check: Look for rewrap code that writes a new wrap without first checking the unwrapped key's size and key check, or that generates new material.

rules.statement: Never remove an existing recovery copy of a key just because recovery is not configured; leave it as it is, and remove it only through an explicit operation that requires it.
rules.why: A recovery path must never be removed silently.
rules.check: Look for rewrap or update code that clears or overwrites the recovery wrap when no recovery public key is configured.

rules.statement: In a batch key-maintenance operation, check required preconditions (such as a configured recovery public key) before reading any row, and make the operation safe to run again so that a repeated run gives the same result as the first.
rules.why: A run should fail before it does any partial work, and an operator must be able to re-run a Job safely.
rules.check: Look for a precondition checked inside the per-row loop rather than before it, or for row handling that changes the result when run a second time.

rules.statement: When a host binary also handles an offline command verb, parse the verb and its arguments first and build the host with the remaining arguments only, so the command-line configuration provider never reads the verb or its arguments.
rules.why: This stops verb arguments, such as a key file path, from leaking into host configuration.
rules.check: Look for the full args array passed to Host.CreateApplicationBuilder or WebApplication.CreateBuilder when the program also handles command verbs.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, mount a Secret that holds an offline-only private key into the one-off Job that needs it and never into the serving Deployment.
rules.why: The serving process must never be able to reach the recovery private key.
rules.check: Look in chart templates for the recovery or offline key Secret mounted or referenced in the Deployment's pod spec.
